text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Increased 5xx rate detected in asia-northeast1 inference cluster (service: /v1/generate). Alert firing on 95th percentile error rate > 2% for 3m. Auto-escalation to oncall. Monitoring: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/1756

alex.m: Oncall here, looking at logs now. Can someone confirm if this is all zones in asia-northeast1 or a single zone?

maria: I see spikes across two AZs (ane1-a, ane1-b). latency also up ~200ms for slow tail. Pulling recent deploys.

jin: No deployments in last 30m, node counts look stable. I suspect networking issue to the egress path to our model hosts in that region.

alex.m: Good call. If it's egress we should failover traffic at the routing layer. Runbook: inference-routing -> region-failover (doc: https://wiki.redwood/inference/failover). Plan: (1) update status page + customer comms, (2) reroute 80% traffic to asia-southeast1, keep 20% for verification, (3) monitor errors & latency, (4) escalate to neteng if still failing.

maria: I'll draft the status page update now. Proposed status snippet: "We are investigating increased error rates for inference requests in asia-northeast1. Customers in APAC may experience higher latencies or failed requests. We are actively rerouting traffic and monitoring. No data loss expected." Want sign-off from oncall.

support-lead: Please include impact matrix: affected regions (asia-northeast1), affected zones (ane1-a, ane1-b), customer tiers (all), mitigation (regional reroute to asia-southeast1), ETA for next update (15m). Also share list of top affected customers so SRE + Support can DM.

alex.m: Agreed. Top affected customers seen in logs: acme-inc (high request volume), edu-platform (medium), tiny-startup (low). Severity: acme-inc likely high impact — prioritize outreach.

jin: I'm going to run the reroute to traffic-router. Command (internal API):
```
curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/route/adjust \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"from_region":"asia-northeast1","to_region":"asia-southeast1","percent":80}'
```
Executing now.

ops-bot: autoscaler:scaledown: ane1-b scaled down 2 nodes at 1756004800 — maybe unrelated but noted.

jin: Reroute command returned 202 Accepted. Router status: applying. Traffic shift progress: 45% -> 80% in 3m. Seeing error rate drop to 0.8% in asia-northeast1 and slight bump in asia-southeast1 to 0.4%.

maria: Draft status page update ready. Posting below for approval:

"We are currently investigating elevated error rates for inference in asia-northeast1. We have initiated a traffic reroute to asia-southeast1 to reduce customer impact. Some requests may experience increased latency while the reroute completes. Our engineers are monitoring and will provide updates every 15 minutes. Affected zones: ane1-a, ane1-b. Impacted customers: selection of high-volume APAC tenants. Mitigation: regional reroute in progress; automatic retries are in place."

Can someone from oncall + support sign off to publish?

support-lead: Sign off from Support for that language. Also propose a short targeted customer note for acme-inc (they pay for SLA):
Subject: Temporary inference degradation in asia-northeast1 — mitigation in progress
Body: Hi team, we're seeing increased errors in asia-northeast1 impacting inference requests. We've rerouted most traffic to asia-southeast1; engineers are monitoring. No data loss is expected. We'll follow up within 30 minutes with status. If you'd like, we can enable a dedicated bypass for your traffic. — Redwood Support

sarah: I can send the DM/email to acme-inc and flagged for priority. Who will publish the public status update?

maria: I'll publish to status.redwood.ai once alex approves the final wording. Draft posted here, ready.

alex.m: Go ahead and publish the status update. Small edit: change "automatic retries are in place" -> "client-side retries may observe reduced success; server-side retries are enabled for internal services." Publish and set next update ETA +15m.

status-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATE: published incident • asia-northeast1 degraded • https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1756004321 • next update at 1756005221

jin: Monitoring after reroute: overall 5xx count down 70% cluster-wide. Latency in ase1 increased by ~50ms for some requests but under SLO for most. Rolling verification shows success rate stable at 99.2% for rerouted traffic.

alex.m: Good. Next: if traffic doesn't stabilize fully in 20m, we escalate to neteng for deeper packet inspection and consider region-wide capacity burst in ase1. Also coordinate with Dedicated ops if any reserved pools are affected.

support-lead: Support has sent targeted emails to acme-inc and edu-platform. Will open DM threads and route any incoming customer reports to this incident thread.

ops-bot: note: backup GPU pool in asia-southeast1 currently at 60% utilization; capacity available for short bursts.

jin: Passing on-call to alex.m for rounding down; I'm staying as second responder. alex.m: do you want a formal handoff?

alex.m: Handoff accepted. Checklist: (1) confirm status page posted, (2) ensure targeted customer notifications sent, (3) monitor for 30m stable window, (4) escalate if >1% 5xx cluster-wide. I'm taking over primary watch. Jin — leave your logs pointers here.

jin: Logs/queries:
- 95p error rate query: `SELECT p95(error_rate) FROM infra.errors WHERE region='asia-northeast1' AND since=now()-5m`
- router audit: https://router.internal/audit/1756004321
- packet captures saved to /var/packets/1756004321.tar.gz (neteng access required)

alex.m: Thanks. I'll update the next status in 15m. If anything changes before then, post here or page.

status-bot: incident note: paging suppressed for non-critical alerts during incident coordination.

support-lead: FYI legal/compliance wants a log dump if we escalate — flagged.

alex.m: Closing loop: as of last check (1756006125) error rate in asia-northeast1 dropped to 0.3%, overall traffic stable. Keeping incident open for postmortem and followups. Next scheduled update 1756007025.

on-message: [this thread contains root message + replies for incident coordination; saved for postmortem reference]
